question: The land administration system is failing. How do we protect the data and replace it, and in what order?

plan.title: I’ll answer
plan.text: How to protect land data and replace the system, in order

plan.title: I’ll look at
plan.text: The 2025 audit, Lands and Surveys reports, two replacement proposals

plan.title: You’ll get
plan.text: Backup first, then open process gaps, then options with risks and a recommended order

answer.summary: The land registry can still be read but is failing under load. Protect the data first, then close the process gaps that let errors in, then replace the system in stages. Doing it in this order keeps title transactions running while the new system is built.

order.title: Back up and verify every record
order.text: Take a full, verified copy off the failing servers and test that it restores. [1]

order.title: Freeze changes to the old system
order.text: Only fixes that protect data. No new features or fields.

order.title: Close the process gaps
order.text: Fix the 2 critical gaps from the audit first, so bad data stops entering. [2]

order.title: Choose a replacement
order.text: Compare the options below with Lands and Surveys and Finance.

order.title: Migrate in stages
order.text: Move parish by parish, running old and new side by side.

sources: Lands and Surveys - System health report, September 2026.pdf
Auditor General - Land registry process audit 2025.pdf
CARICOM - Regional land information platform brief.docx

options.name: Repair and extend
options.text: Keep the current system and patch it. Cheapest now, risky later.

options.name: Off-the-shelf registry
options.text: Proven product, configured for Barbados. 9 to 12 months.

options.name: Shared regional platform
options.text: Join a CARICOM land platform. Lower cost, less control.

answer.recommendation: My recommendation: back up this week, then take the off-the-shelf route. It balances speed and control, and Finance already budgeted for it in the 2026 Estimates [3]. Repairing the old system only buys time.
